question: Regulation (EU) 2017/1939 provides that the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) is granted investigation and prosecution powers and that its independence and accountability to the Union institutions are to be ensured by institutional safeguards. To this end, the European Chief Prosecutor reports to the European Parliament annually on the EPPO’s work.

During a 9 April 2024 parliamentary hearing on the 2023 activity report, European Chief Prosecutor Laura Codruța Kövesi said, in response to a question on the state of play of investigations into the Pfizergate allegations, that there were ‘no suspects’ at that time.

1 The author of this question has since come into possession of the cover page of a court file created in 2023 entitled ‘VON DER LEYEN Ursula’, as well as the cover page of an investigation report by Belgium’s central anti-corruption bureau (Office central pour la répression de la corruption – OCCRC), in which Ursula von der Leyen and Albert Bourla are mentioned. 1.
When was the Commission informed by the EPPO that a judicial investigation relating to the President of the Commission was under way?
What is the Commission’s assessment of the European Chief Prosecutor’s remarks on 9 April 2024 in the light of the aforementioned documents?
Is the Commission aware that judicial proceedings against the European Chief Prosecutor are pending in this connection?

The Annual Report 2023 of the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) CJ09/9/05138, Presentation by Laura Kövesi, the European Chief Prosecutor, giving account of the general activities of the EPPO to the European Parliament [Article 7 Council Regulation (EU) 2017/1939] https://multimedia.europarl.europa.eu/en/webstreaming/joint-committee-on-budgetary-control-andcommittee-on-civil-liberties-justice-and-home-affairs_20240409-1430-COMMITTEE-CONT-LIBE. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.10.2026) The Commission has learned from an article in the Belgian newspaper Le Vif of 13 April 20231 that a Belgian citizen has filed a criminal complaint with a juge d’instruction in Liège against the President of the Commission.

A subsequent article in the same newspaper, dated 14 July 2023, quotes a spokesperson of the European Public Prosecutor Office (EPPO) as saying that the EPPO had registered the criminal complaint and was in contact with the Belgian authorities2. The procedure concluded with a judgment by the Court of Appeal of Liège of 20 January 2025, by which the Court of Appeal declared inadmissible the criminal complaint.

The Belgian Court of Cassation confirmed the inadmissibility of the criminal complaint by judgment of 22 October 2025. The Commission has no comment on the remark of the European Chief Prosecutor to which the Honourable Member refers. The Commission does not comment on allegedly ongoing judicial proceedings against other institutions or bodies.
